1. **Lekkerkerker, C. G.** (1951-1952). Voorstelling van natuurlijke getallen door een som van getallen van Fibonacci. *Simon Stevin*, 29:190--195.

2. **Zeckendorf, E.** (1972). Représentation des nombres naturels par une somme de nombres de Fibonacci ou de nombres de Lucas. *Bulletin de la société royale des sciences de Liège*, 41, 179–182.
   - [Source](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89douard_Zeckendorf)

3. **Hoggatt, V. E., Jr.** (1972). The Generalized Zeckendorf Theorem. *The Fibonacci Quarterly*, 10(1), 92-97.
   - [Source](https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/10-1/hoggatt2.pdf)

4. **Knuth, D.** (1988). Fibonacci Multiplication. *Applied Mathematics Letters*, 1(1), 57-60.
   - [Source](https://math.osu.edu/sites/math.osu.edu/files/henderson_zeckendorf.pdf)

5. **Frougny, C., & Sakarovitch, J.** ([9]). A finite two-tape automaton converting Zeckendorf expansion into Bergman representation.
   - [Source](https://kr.mirrors.cicku.me/ctan/macros/generic/zeckendorf/zeckendorf-doc.pdf)

6. **Shallit, J.** ([10]). Revisiting the Frougny-Sakarovitch automaton for converting Zeckendorf expansions into Bergman representations.
   - [Source](https://jp.mirrors.cicku.me/ctan/macros/generic/zeckendorf/zeckendorf-doc.pdf)

These references discuss various aspects of Zeckendorf representations, including their existence, uniqueness, and conversions to other representations.

Announcement text:

This adds many new features and has some breaking changes due to renamings, not listed here.
* It is not \xintiieval but \xinteval's syntax which is now extended.
* Variables phi and psi are defined and one can do algebra with +, -, *, and ^ on them in Q(phi).
* The Bergman phi-representation is added for elements of Z[phi] in particular for integers.
* The $ character doing the Knuth Fibonacci multiplication on positive integers now uses the (more efficient) Arnoux formula. The $$ computes out of deference according to the Knuth formula.
* The PDF documentation section on the mathematical background has been extended and includes bibliographical references.
* The interactive interface integrates all novelties.

Summary description: Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers

Announcement text:

This adds many new features and has some breaking changes due to renamings, not listed here.
* It is not \xintiieval but \xinteval's syntax which is now extended.
* Variables phi and psi are defined and one can do algebra with +, -, *, and ^ on them in Q(phi).
* The Bergman phi-representation is added for elements of Z[phi] in particular for integers.
* The $ character doing the Knuth Fibonacci multiplication on positive integers now uses the (more efficient) Arnoux formula. The $$ computes out of deference according to the Knuth formula.
* The PDF documentation section on the mathematical background has been extended and includes bibliographical references.
* The interactive interface integrates all novelties.
The package’s Catalogue entry can be viewed at https://ctan.org/pkg/zeckendorf
The package’s files themselves can be inspected at https://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/generic/zeckendorf/

Historical Note

William Zeckendorf (1905-1976) was a prominent American real estate developer. Through his development company Webb and Knapp, Inc.—for which he began working in 1938 and which he purchased in 1949—he developed a significant portion of the New York City urban landscape. In the 1960s, Webb and Knapp filed for bankruptcy protection.
Return to Top

Content Description

The collection contains fourteen pieces of correspondence for 1946 and 1968 (including items from Nelson A. Rockefeller); blueprints for a partially submerged garage at Robert R. Young Village, New York; and six magazine and newspaper articles about Zeckendorf.

V.E.HOGGATTJR.
San Jose State College, Sao Jose, California
DEDICATED TO DR. E. ZECKENDORF
1. INTRODUCTION
The Zeckendorf theorem states that every positive integer can be
uniquely represented as the sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers if no two con-
secutive Fibonacci numbers are used in any given sum.
D. E. Daykin [1] proved the converse of the Zeckendorf theorem.
Keller [2] generalized the Zeckendorf theorem and proved a restricted con-
verse for monotone increasing integer sequences. Hence we generalize the
Zeckendorf theorem in a different way and also get a restricted converse.
This leaves two open questions as to validity of the unrestricted converse
theorems.
